scope: Trial cross-room WOL send attempts using saved room/IP/MAC, without changes to network infrastructure.
verified: All four explicit wake modes derive concrete endpoints; UDP9 is fixed.
Private IPv4 and one concrete saved room only; empty/public/local/special/network/broadcast/duplicate targets rejected.
Plan snapshots targets; entire batch validated before network socket creation.
Directed broadcast uses actual configured prefix; duplicate directed/local destinations collapse.
At most three 102-byte magic packets per path; routed TTL16 versus local broadcast TTL1.
Real UDP loopback confirms exact packet bytes and TTL without contacting classroom devices.
Partial path failure preserves counts and other explicit attempts; cancellation stops subsequent packets/routes.
UI loads original roster without send; defaults unicast and /24; confirmation lists saved identities and destination addresses.
Selection and whole-room scopes, cancellation, result wording and trial version navigation checked.
Startup still requests no child processes; default apps, cleanup kernel, old same-subnet WOL and power dispatch unchanged.
limitations: Not tested on real classroom networks or Windows NIC sleep/off states.
IP reachability while powered on does not prove WOL delivery after shutdown.
Unicast depends on gateway neighbor state and NIC support; directed/local broadcasts depend on existing forwarding/broadcast domains.
Saved IP/MAC relationship is not directly ARP-verified across subnets.
No switch/router/firewall/ARP/IP settings are modified; no relay agent is installed.
UDP handoff is not a delivery or wake confirmation.
environment_helpers: Byte-identical to v0.6.4; not retested because unchanged.
screenshots: Synthetic classroom records and injected send result, not evidence of real machine wake.
